newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Ansett, SIA no comment on equity link.
newsitem.headline: Ansett, SIA no comment on equity link.

text.p: Ansett Airlines and Singapore Airlines refused to speculate about the possibility of Singapore Airlines taking a stake in Ansett after the two, along with Air New Zealand, announced an operations alliance on Friday.

"There has been a lot of speculation about a possible equity relationship between ourselves (and Singapore Airlines) at sometime in the future. This is not an appropriate time to talk about that," Ansett's managing director Rod Eddington told a news conference held jointly by the three airlines.
"We are here today to talk about commercial cooperation," he said.
Eddington said the memorandum of understanding the three airlines had signed today was not the final contract but that it committed the three to negotiating the alliance.

"Such an alliance will need approval from the appropriate regulators but we are confident that we can demonstrate to these regulators that our proposed joint activity will provide tangible benefits to the travelling public," he said.
Eddington said Ansett would not cut staff as a result of the alliance but rather the long term effects of the alliance was a growth opportunity for the three carriers.
"It will enable us to be more competitive by combining our activities in a few key areas. It will allow us to be more efficient," he said.
One clear area where the three airlines would benefit from the alliance was in using their combined purchasing power to get better deals from aircraft manufacturers, Eddington said.
